title: Wine Wimsey Review · Oct 27
subtitle: 16 feed (14 images + 2 TOBIs at #4 and #9) and 4 stories, for posting Tue Oct 27 · 12 image posts recreated from your inbox screenshots (quotes word for word, one emoji dropped on the grown-kids quote, the dog stays in the dog quote) · 2 fresh image posts, 2 TOBIs and 4 stories written new and checked against the used list · 7 Hot Mess and 7 Homebody

posts.quote: Menopause has turned me into someone who needs a nap because I couldn’t sleep last night. But I can’t take a nap because I might not sleep tonight.
posts.caption: Tuesday at 2 p.m. I sat on the edge of the bed with every intention of a twenty-minute rest. I looked at the pillow. The pillow looked at me. Then I got up and folded a towel instead, because some part of my brain has decided that daytime sleep is a trap. By evening I was so tired I could hear the refrigerator humming a lullaby. I'm not saying it's a system with flaws. I'm saying it's a system, and I live inside it.
posts.first: I tried lavender, a fan, and a very boring podcast about bridges. The podcast came closest. I fell asleep at minute eleven, woke up at minute twelve, and the bridge was still going. I'm told it's a good bridge.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a yawning woman with pink curls hugging a pillow on the edge of a bed, a glass of red wine and an alarm clock on the nightstand. Text at the top reads: Menopause has turned me into someone who needs a nap because I couldn’t sleep last night. But I can’t take a nap because I might not sleep tonight.

posts.quote: You’re over 35. Better go pee before you leave, pee when you get there, pee while you’re there, and pee before you leave.
posts.caption: My car now has a mental map of every bathroom within twenty miles. I know which ones have a line and which ones lock properly. It's the most useful knowledge I own.
posts.first: Last month I stopped at a gas station, a library and a garden center on a single twenty-minute drive. I bought a cactus at the last one out of gratitude. It's thriving, which is more than I can say for my dignity.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman in a hallway with car keys, legs crossed and wincing, hurrying toward an open bathroom door, a glass of red wine on a hall table. Text at the top reads: You’re over 35. Better go pee before you leave, pee when you get there, pee while you’re there, and pee before you leave.

posts.quote: I wish I were as tired in the middle of the night as I am in the middle of the day.
posts.caption: At 3:17 this morning I was wide awake thinking about a casserole I made in 2009. Full detail, no skipped steps. By two the next afternoon my eyelids were doing their best impression of garage doors. I'd love to swap the schedule. Give me the sleepy hours at night and the bright ones at noon, and I'll do wonders. Until then I'll keep a mug close and a blanket closer, and call it a lifestyle.
posts.first: I did the math on my coffee last week and decided never to do it again. My doctor says it's fine. My husband says it's a personality. I say it's the only thing standing between me and the casserole thoughts.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a wide-eyed woman with pink curls sitting on the edge of a bed at night holding a glass of red wine, a bedside clock reading 3:17 and a moonlit window. Text at the top reads: I wish I were as tired in the middle of the night as I am in the middle of the day.

posts.quote: Some days my whole personality is a good mug and low expectations.
posts.first: My favorite mug has a chip in the handle and a tiny crack near the bottom. I've had it eleven years and nothing has ever tasted better. Low expectations are underrated. They've never once let me down.

posts.quote: I didn’t grow up with having my feelings validated, safe spaces, or gentle parenting. I grew up with... FIX YOUR FACE OR I’LL FIX IT FOR YOU.
posts.caption: Nobody in my house ever asked how I felt about anything. We were asked whether we'd finished our plate and whether we were planning to keep that expression. Somehow we all turned out fine, mostly, and with excellent timing for a stern look. I can freeze a room at forty paces. It isn't a skill I chose. It's an inheritance, like the good silver and a deep suspicion of leftovers.
posts.first: My mother still does it. I'll say something mildly sad on the phone and she'll say 'well, eat something.' It's her love language and I've stopped fighting it. I sit down, eat the thing, and feel better every time, which annoys me enormously.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a stern woman in a vintage kitchen holding a glass of red wine and pointing a finger at the viewer, a casserole dish and wooden spoon on the counter. Text at the top reads: I didn’t grow up with having my feelings validated, safe spaces, or gentle parenting. I grew up with... FIX YOUR FACE OR I’LL FIX IT FOR YOU.

posts.quote: When old people say “Enjoy them while they’re young” they are talking about your hips and knees, not your kids.
posts.caption: Somewhere around fifty I started getting out of chairs in three separate stages. The porch swing is the one seat that never gives me trouble, so that's where I live now.
posts.first: My grandfather used to say it every time we came over, and I was sure it was about us. Turns out he was warning me. I wish he'd been more specific. I'd have started stretching in my thirties.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with pink curls in a rocking chair on an autumn porch holding a glass of red wine, one hand on her hip, with a knowing smile. Text at the top reads: When old people say “Enjoy them while they’re young” they are talking about your hips and knees, not your kids.

posts.quote: Shoutout to everyone who can’t keep up with the laundry or the dishes but decided it was a great idea to start gardening.
posts.caption: I have five baskets of clean laundry I haven't folded and a sink that's been waiting since Sunday. On Saturday I bought four tomato plants, two herbs and a bag of soil that weighs more than a toddler. It felt like the right call at the time. The garden looks great. The house is a story for another day, and I'll tell it after I finish this glass and these seedlings.
posts.first: My neighbor stopped by with a compliment on the tomatoes and glanced through the window at the laundry mountain. She said nothing, which is the nicest thing a neighbor can do. I gave her a basil plant. We're good.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a satisfied woman in muddy boots holding a glass of red wine in a messy kitchen with a laundry pile, dirty dishes and seedling pots. Text at the top reads: Shoutout to everyone who can’t keep up with the laundry or the dishes but decided it was a great idea to start gardening.

posts.quote: My grown kids have started giving me advice, which is cute... considering I kept them alive before Google.
posts.caption: Last Sunday my kids both called with tips. One told me which app to use for my calendar. The other forwarded an article about getting more steps. I thanked them sweetly and kept rinsing the wine glass I'd been enjoying. They really do mean well. They're just so confident, and I remember very clearly when they couldn't find their own shoes. I'll keep that memory handy for a rainy day.
posts.first: My son texted last night to remind me to drink water. I sent back a photo of my glass. It was water. Mostly. He wrote 'proud of you,' and I'll admit it made my whole evening.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of an amused woman with pink curls holding a glass of red wine leaning on a kitchen counter, two grown children behind her gesturing with phones. Text at the top reads: My grown kids have started giving me advice, which is cute... considering I kept them alive before Google.

posts.quote: My inner child wants a nap. My inner adult wants a nap. Finally, we agree.
posts.first: That's the only time they've agreed in years. I took it as a sign and went to find a blanket. It lasted forty minutes, and I'd call it the most productive meeting I've ever attended.

posts.quote: When a teenager shows up at your door on Halloween, please don’t make them feel too old to trick-or-treat. Smile, say hello, and give them the candy. Because childhood doesn’t last forever, and there’s absolutely no reason to rush them out of it.
posts.caption: Every year somebody tall with a deep voice rings my bell and holds out a pillowcase. Every year I give him the good candy. Nobody leaves my porch with a pillowcase full of nothing.
posts.first: A few years ago a teenager thanked me and then said, a little shyly, that he almost didn't come this year. I gave him a second handful. I think about that doorstep moment every October, and I always keep a few full-size bars for the last bell.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a smiling woman at her open front door holding a bowl of candy for a tall teenager in a hoodie with a pillowcase, a jack-o'-lantern on the porch. Text at the top reads: When a teenager shows up at your door on Halloween, please don’t make them feel too old to trick-or-treat. Smile, say hello, and give them the candy. Because childhood doesn’t last forever, and there’s absolutely no reason to rush them out of it.

posts.quote: I stay hydrated by adding ice to my wine. Follow me for more classy health tips.
posts.caption: There's a bag of ice in my freezer for exactly one purpose, and it isn't injuries. I keep three bags in the summer and I'm not apologizing.
posts.first: My sister-in-law gasped when I did it at her cookout. By dessert she had a glass of her own with two cubes and a very guilty smile. I didn't say a word. The ice said everything.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with pink curls proudly dropping an ice cube into a glass of red wine in a kitchen, a bowl of ice and a wine bottle on the counter. Text at the top reads: I stay hydrated by adding ice to my wine. Follow me for more classy health tips.

posts.quote: If only dogs could drop off irresponsible owners on the side of the road—now that would be justice.
posts.caption: There's a dog in my neighborhood who always looks like the smartest being on the block, and I'm convinced he's judging us from his window. Last week I watched him lean out and bark at a delivery truck that had blocked the driveway. He was right to. I stood on the sidewalk and nodded. Sometimes a dog just says what everyone's thinking, and I respect it.
posts.first: My own mother taught me that how a person treats an animal tells you all you need to know. I've never found a reason to doubt it. I plan to keep a cookie in my pocket for that dog every day until he graduates.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of an indignant woman on a country roadside while a smug golden retriever sits at the wheel of a small blue car, a man with a suitcase left on the shoulder behind them. Text at the top reads: If only dogs could drop off irresponsible owners on the side of the road—now that would be justice.

posts.quote: Walmart thinks I want to put up my Christmas tree and eat turkey while wearing my Halloween costume.
posts.caption: I walked in for dish soap and walked past three seasons of decorations in one aisle. Nobody else seemed alarmed, so I bought the soap and kept moving.
posts.first: Last week they had pumpkins next to a nine-foot snowman and a rack of sparkly party hats. I stood there holding my cart like I'd lost my place in time. A kind employee asked if I needed help. I said no, but thanked her anyway.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a bewildered woman with pink curls in a store aisle with a cart, shelves crowded with pumpkins, a Christmas tree, a roasted turkey and a witch hat, a bottle of red wine in the cart. Text at the top reads: Walmart thinks I want to put up my Christmas tree and eat turkey while wearing my Halloween costume.

posts.quote: Brain cells die. Skin cells die, and even hair cells die. But the fat cells in my stomach must have accepted Jesus Christ as their Lord and Savior since they seem to have eternal life.
posts.caption: My doctor says everything in the body renews itself. Skin, nails, even the lining of the stomach. I asked about the part that sits right over it and he laughed longer than I expected. I've made peace with it. We've been through two kids, three diets and a bad winter together. Some friendships are just that durable, and I do appreciate the loyalty.
posts.first: I told my sister the joke over the phone and she snorted her coffee. Then she admitted she had her own theory involving cheese. We agreed to lunch. No salad was mentioned, and none was invited.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman lounging on a couch with a bowl of chips and a glass of red wine, looking fondly down at her belly, a blanket and remote beside her. Text at the top reads: Brain cells die. Skin cells die, and even hair cells die. But the fat cells in my stomach must have accepted Jesus Christ as their Lord and Savior since they seem to have eternal life.

posts.quote: I put on real shoes today. Nobody noticed, but I’m taking the rest of the day to recover.
posts.caption: The shoes had laces and everything. I found them in the back of the closet where I'd put them in March. They were very surprised to see me.
posts.first: I wore them to the mailbox and back. It was eleven steps each way. My husband said I looked great. I said I felt like I'd run a marathon, and we both agreed it was a fair review.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of an exhausted woman with pink curls slumped in an armchair wearing one sneaker and one slipper, a glass of red wine on the side table. Text at the top reads: I put on real shoes today. Nobody noticed, but I’m taking the rest of the day to recover.

posts.quote: I made a to-do list so I’d feel productive. Then I added “make a to-do list” just so I could cross something off.
posts.caption: On Monday I sat down with my coffee and wrote a list of nine things. Taxes, the dentist, the garage, the casserole dish I borrowed in June. By noon I'd done none of them and added four more. Then I wrote 'make a list' at the very bottom and crossed it out with the flourish of someone who has been to college. Productivity is mostly about how it looks on paper, and on paper I'm doing wonderfully.
posts.first: I keep the list on the fridge with a magnet shaped like a lemon. My daughter looked at it and said, 'Mom, this is just a list of lists.' I'm taking it as a compliment. It's the most organized thing I've ever made.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman at a kitchen table with a long handwritten list, crossing off one line with a flourish, a glass of red wine beside her. Text at the top reads: I made a to-do list so I’d feel productive. Then I added “make a to-do list” just so I could cross something off.

stories.quote: A glass of wine tastes better when you finally sit down to drink it.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a relieved woman sitting down in an armchair with a glass of red wine, shoes kicked off. Text at the top reads: A glass of wine tastes better when you finally sit down to drink it.

stories.quote: Fall is for boots, soup, and a very serious relationship with my slippers.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with pink curls stirring a pot of soup in a warm kitchen, boots by the door, fluffy slippers on her feet. Text at the top reads: Fall is for boots, soup, and a very serious relationship with my slippers.

stories.quote: “I’m tired” is a full sentence, and you don’t owe anyone the rest.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a calm woman on a couch with a blanket and a glass of red wine, a phone face down on the coffee table. Text at the top reads: “I’m tired” is a full sentence, and you don’t owe anyone the rest.

stories.quote: Some days the win is simply wearing pants with a zipper.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a proud woman with pink curls holding up a pair of jeans at her bedroom mirror, a glass of red wine on the dresser. Text at the top reads: Some days the win is simply wearing pants with a zipper.
